governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.
Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching; keep non-external CLI/API work under 50ms.
Update affected documentation—especially `src/intent/*`—without changing its established format.
Use installed coding-agent CLIs for coding-agent capabilities; do not reimplement them.

findings.description: The plan equates cached checkout HEAD with the commit embodied by the running executable, but ./r runs bin/refine and the checkout can move after that binary was built while the hourly cache still appears fresh, so Running from HEAD or current could remain false.
findings.recommendation: Record or verify the running binary's source commit, compare live checkout HEAD with the cached local identity, and report unknown on any provenance or cache mismatch.

result.summary: The plan needs an authoritative boundary between the running executable, live checkout HEAD, and cached upstream evidence.

checklist.description: Extend the existing host runtime-status capability to classify the bootstrap-owned running executable as a validated published release or source build and expose immutable source-commit provenance recorded with that executable separately from the product home's live checkout HEAD.

Combine the running executable commit, live checkout HEAD, and cached local and upstream identities into a fail-closed source relationship that reports running from HEAD and current, behind, ahead, or diverged only when provenance matches and the cache is fresh, otherwise reporting the specific status as unknown.

Revise the shared upgrade-status API contract so validated published releases retain version and upgrade fields while source runtimes return the structured executable, checkout, upstream, freshness, and relationship status consumed by surfaces.

Update the shared Node tab-strip banner used above Processes to preserve Running latest and Upgrade available for validated published releases while rendering source runtimes as Running from HEAD with their trustworthy upstream relationship or an honest unknown state.
Update the affected Process and browser intent pages to document the published-release validation boundary, running-executable provenance, cached upstream evidence, and unknown-state behavior.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: The revised plan records immutable source-commit provenance with the running executable, compares it with the live checkout HEAD and the cached local identity, and permits a HEAD or upstream-current claim only when all identities agree and the upstream cache is fresh, with every provenance, freshness, or identity mismatch reported as unknown.

result.summary: Make Node > Processes distinguish a validated published release from a source-built runtime, and describe a source runtime as running from HEAD or current with upstream only when the running executable's immutable source commit agrees with the live checkout and fresh cached upstream evidence.

governance_precheck.message: The finalized plan does not require any governance violation.

checklist.evidence: Added build.rs metadata that embeds the observed Git commit, records exact-source status only for a clean matching checkout, and records a release tag only when that exact commit carries the package-version tag. Source-promotion candidate builds fence the requested commit through REFINE_BUILD_SOURCE_COMMIT. Added the cohesive src/tools/host/runtime_status.rs host capability so executable provenance remains separate from the bootstrap-owned live checkout.

Extended cached source snapshots with current, behind, ahead, and diverged ancestry. Runtime status permits Running from HEAD and an upstream relationship only when executable commit, live checkout HEAD, both cached identities, cached snapshot identities, recognized ancestry, and fresh cache all agree; stale, missing, dirty-build, or mismatched evidence returns a stable specific unknown_reason.

Replaced the page-local /upgrade inference with FileRuntimeStatusService. Validated published_release responses retain current_version, latest_version, available, and upgrade_available; source responses expose structured executable, checkout, upstream, freshness, relationship, running_from_head, and unknown_reason fields without fetching or adopting request CWD.

Updated the shared runtime banner above Node tabs: published releases still render Running latest or Upgrade available, while source runtimes render Running from HEAD with current/behind/ahead/diverged upstream text only for trusted evidence, otherwise an honest reason-specific unknown state. Added browser-unit coverage for every relationship and the unknown path.

Updated docs/intent/03-capabilities/01-process.md, docs/intent/04-surfaces/03-browser/17-processes.md, and docs/intent/04-surfaces/04-api.md with the release validation boundary, immutable executable provenance, cached upstream proof, structured API, and fail-closed unknown behavior while preserving the established intent format.
